steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Layer 1/2 of the potatoes, 1/2 of the ham, and 1/2 of the onions in a 2-quart baking dish; repeat layers.
Cook milk, peas, flour, butter, parsley, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and onion powder in a saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until thickened, 7 to 10 minutes.
Stir Cheddar cheese into sauce until melted.
Pour sauce over potato and ham mixture; sprinkle with paprika. Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until potatoes are tender, about 1 hour. Remove foil and continue baking until lightly browned, about 15 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheesy Scalloped Potatoes with Ham
raw_recipe.description: This scalloped potatoes and ham casserole is cooked with onions and green peas in a cheesy, herby white sauce for the ultimate comfort food dinner.
raw_recipe.name: Cheesy Scalloped Potatoes with Ham

review.reviewBody: The taste was really good and the meal was filling. However, it took more than 2 hours to cook rather than 1 hr and 15 minutes. I suggest cooking the potatoes and then, make the dish. If it had not been for that, I would have given five stars..

I subbed a little. Baked hash brown rounds 3/4 done while sautéing onion and garlic. Cook over half way. Add frozen veggies. Sauté About 1 minute. Add flour and spices to veggies when onion 3/4 translucent And mix well. Add milk/cheese mix to veggie mix. Only Colby/jack and frozen broc/cauli/carrot mix on hand. 
Mash taters a little, layer ham, spoon spread liquid/ mix, cover with foil and an hr later put the cheese on for 15 mins. YUM! Those flavors were amazing together. It’s on rotation after ham night which makes me want ham night more often! Doing cheddar next time.

Had leftover ham from Thanksgiving that I used. I used all ingredients but I alternate the roux making process. I melted the butter and added equal part flour, then added the milk, cheese, and seasoning. I added the peas in the layering process. It was tasty.

Great recipe but instructions need tweaking. Firstly, the peas should be scattered among the layers, not mixed in the sauce because after pouring over the potato mixture, they just sit on top and get browned during baking. Also, the sauce should start with melting the butter then whisking in the flour and gradually adding the milk/spices until thickened. Otherwise a great recipe!

A good start as written, but needs some work. I microwaved the sliced potatoes for 2 mins. before assembling the dish, then baked @ 375 for 1 hr. covered & 15 minutes uncovered. The dish was perfect at that point. The sauce tasted a little bland, so I added some Dijon mustard & Worcestershire Sauce.

This turned out wonderful! I did leave out the peas. I did melt the butter first, added the flour and then the milk instead of putting them all in at once. I will admit I forgot to add the cheese but I added it after it was all baked, put it back in the oven for a couple of minutes for it to melt and then stirred it all together. It still turned out great! We all had seconds and my doubting husband admitted he really like it! Thank you!

Was excellent and easy! Followed recipe exactly for the cheese sauce. I happened to have 3 cans of white sliced potatoes in my pantry and used those instead of raw potatoes. Worked very well and cut down the baking time. Baked for 25 min. with tin foil on. Removed foil, added a handful of cracker crumbs on top and baked another 15 min. The cracker crumbs were a nice addition.
Used 2% milk and it turned out watery. Next time will use while milk and more cheese. Will extend cooking time by 15 minutes. Great flavor!
I added all the scrap cheese - cheddar, Swiss. I’m gluten free and used corn starch instead of flour. It turned out great!

Had some leftover ham from Easter and we always enjoy making scalloped potatoes and ham. This was different than our usual recipe and I can say we will be using from now on. Used the original recipe except did not put peas in it and added a pinch of cayenne pepper. Based on other reviews I did turn the oven on to 400 degrees and baked it for about an hour and 10 minutes then removed the cover for about another 15 minutes. The result was a creamy moist and flavorful meal. We loved it!
I added more milk, more cheese..cooked it all day in a crock pot.....delicious!!!!!
It was awesome!!....I did cornstarch instead of flour and added more milk to pan....added smoked paprika on top it was delicious!!!...will make again...
I have made this several times and it has always been a hit!
Loved it!
I t was won and real easy to prepare

It turned out great and directions were easy to follow. Cook time was accurate. The only thing I would change for next time is to use ham steak portions instead of diced ham. It had a nice flavor and consistency.

I did skip the peas as I did not have any on hand. Tip: I combined the shredded cheese and the dry ingredients except the paprika in a plastic bag and shook it well. I added it to the melted butter & warm milk, stirring every 2 mins. till thick and poured it over the sliced potatoes & onions. Followed direction from there. I plan to use all the dry ingredients to make Broccoli & Potato Soup down the road!

Used up frozen ham from Easter. Followed the recipe except for had no milk so used evaporated. I think it made it creamier. Also did not have any fresh potatoes used canned whole and sliced. ( we just got home from a trip) so it not take that long to bake. The family loved it. I think the white sauce would also make awesome scalloped potatoes.

I aimed to make this a meal on its own with left over Easter ham and reading the reviews I made some changes which made it delicious. I doubled the seasonings and used frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas. I also added a 1/2 cup of cubed velveeta and a 1/2 tablespoon of chicken bullion powder to the milk sauce then baked at 400 for 1 hour.

I also found this to be really very good. But at 350 it took 2 hours to cook. We ended up making sandwiches and chips for dinner because everyone was too hungry. So... I finished cooking it, and it turned out great, just way too long to cook. I agree with misseewatson- either cook the potatoes first, or bake on a higher temp, or allow at least 2 hours cook time at 350.
